source_text:
# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, on purpose (see qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook's own
# "being clever" note and .claude/skills/hecks_qa/SKILL.md's "Authoring a
# new stress domain" section).
#
# TWO THINGS THIS DOMAIN IS FOR, BOTH NEW TO THE CORPUS:
#
# 1. A GENUINELY NESTED PIECE — "a piece nested inside a piece" (ADR 0026's
#    own words), i.e. `entity "Card"` declared INSIDE `entity "Board"`
#    declared inside `aggregate "Workspace"`. `EntityBuilder#entity_impl`
#    has supported this since ADR 0026 landed, and the ONLY place it is
#    actually exercised anywhere in this repository is the language's own
#    self-describing meta-bluebook, `lib/hecks/language/bluebook/
#    process_manager.bluebook` (`entity "Handler"` containing `entity
#    "Dispatch"`) — used for grammar/glossary tooling, never fuzzed, never
#    dispatched through a real running domain. Not one example
#    (pizzas/banking/chess/roster/...) or existing qa/stress_domains
#    entry (ledger_ordering) declares two levels of entity nesting. This
#    domain does, on purpose, to find out whether `bin/project_rust`'s
#    codegen and the differential fuzz harness even handle a SECOND hop
#    correctly — a construct-combination genuinely absent from every
#    fuzzed domain until now.
#
# 2. A NEW-DEPTH CONFIRMATION OF BUG#3's FIX (PR #526, merged) — before
#    the fix, `EntityElement#element_of` coerced an offered addressing
#    identity through its OWN declared type, invariant included, BEFORE
#    ever checking whether any stored element matches it. An identity
#    that failed its own invariant (e.g. `LedgerSequence`'s "a ledger
#    sequence is positive", offered as `0`) raised `InvariantViolation`
#    in Ruby where Rust's own generated `extract_wants` (a raw scalar
#    read, never a typed rebuild) always answered `NotFound` — a genuine
#    Ruby/Rust divergence. PR #526 fixed it generically, in `element_of`
#    itself, which `locate_chain` calls once per hop — meaning the fix
#    SHOULD be hop-depth-agnostic by construction, but nothing had ever
#    actually exercised a second hop to confirm that rather than assume
#    it. `Card.identified_by :sequence` is `CardSequence`, positive-only,
#    deliberately the same shape as the original finding — `Card.Annotate`
#    addressed by a nonexistent, invariant-failing sequence is the SAME
#    bug, at hop TWO (`Workspace` -> `Board` -> `Card`) instead of hop
#    one. `Board.Label`, addressed by a non-blank but invariant-failing
#    `BoardNumber` (`0`, never positive — `to:`'s own routing envelope
#    already refuses a BLANK entity identity before coercion is ever
#    reached, so the addressing type has to be able to fail its
#    invariant on something non-empty; a String "referenced" invariant
#    like `LedgerOrdering`'s own can't), is the identical shape one hop
#    shallower, so both depths are exercised, not just the new one — see
#    this domain's own NOTES.md for what each dispatch confirms and what
#    does not.
Hecks.bluebook "NestedPieces" do
  vision "A workspace holding boards, each holding cards — two real levels of entity nesting, stressing whether the addressing-identity-vs-existence ordering question (BUG#3) recurs at a hop this corpus has never actually reached before."

  core

  aggregate "Workspace" do
    description "A workspace holding boards; each board holds cards."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference, WorkspaceReference
    attribute :boards,    list_of(Board)

    value_object "WorkspaceReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a workspace is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Start a workspace"

      attribute :reference, WorkspaceReference

      emits "WorkspaceOpened"
    end

    command "AddBoard" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Add a board to the workspace"

      reference_to Workspace
      attribute :number, BoardNumber

      sets :boards, append: { number: :number }

      emits "BoardAdded"
    end

    # THE HOP-ONE ADDRESSING TYPE — positive only, same shape as
    # `CardSequence` below, deliberately: a STRING "is referenced"
    # invariant (like `LedgerOrdering`'s own `SlipReference`) can only
    # ever fail on an EMPTY value, and `Routing#envelope` already refuses
    # a blank entity identity before any typed coercion runs at all
    # (`to: contains a blank entity identity`) — so a string identity
    # type can never reach `EntityElement#element_of`'s own coercion step
    # while failing its invariant. A positive-only integer can: `"0"` is
    # non-blank (passes routing) and still fails `BoardNumber`'s own
    # invariant once `element_of` tries to build it.
    value_object "BoardNumber" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a board number is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "BoardLabel" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a board label is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # THE HOP-TWO ADDRESSING TYPE — positive only, so `sequence.value=0`
    # (or negative) is guaranteed to fail its own invariant, exactly the
    # shape `LedgerSequence` (BUG#3's original finding) already is.
    value_object "CardSequence" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a card sequence is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "CardNote" do
      attribute :text, String
    end

    entity "Board" do
      description "One board in the workspace, holding cards."

      identified_by :number

      attribute :number, BoardNumber
      attribute :label,  BoardLabel, optional: true
      attribute :cards,  list_of(Card)

      command "AddCard" do
        role "Owner"
        goal "Add a card to the board"

        attribute :sequence, CardSequence

        sets :cards, append: { sequence: :sequence }

        emits "CardAdded"
      end

      # THE HOP-ONE CONFIRMATION COMMAND. Dispatch this against a
      # `board.number` that does not exist AND fails `BoardNumber`'s own
      # invariant (`0`, never positive) — answers `NotFound` post-fix
      # (`spec/nested_pieces_spec.rb`), the same single-hop shape BUG#3
      # was originally found on `Banking::Account.LedgerEntry.Amend`,
      # confirmed here in a new business shape.
      command "Label" do
        role "Owner"
        goal "Label the board"

        attribute :label, BoardLabel

        sets :label

        emits "BoardLabeled"
      end

      # S17, ADR 0026 — A PIECE NESTED INSIDE A PIECE. `Card` lives entirely
      # inside `Board`, never addressable except through it — the second
      # hop `locate_chain` walks (`EntityElement#element_of`, called once
      # per hop, `owner` becoming `Board` and `container` becoming the
      # just-located `Board` element by the time THIS entity's own command
      # is reached).
      entity "Card" do
        description "One card on the board, with a sequence that must be positive."

        identified_by :sequence

        attribute :sequence, CardSequence
        attribute :note,     CardNote, optional: true

        # THE HOP-TWO CONFIRMATION COMMAND — THE WHOLE REASON THIS DOMAIN
        # EXISTS. Dispatch this against a `card.sequence` that does not
        # exist AND fails `CardSequence`'s own invariant (`0` or negative)
        # — answers `NotFound` post-fix (`spec/nested_pieces_spec.rb`),
        # confirming BUG#3's fix generalizes one hop deeper than anywhere
        # it had actually been exercised before this domain existed.
        command "Annotate" do
          role "Owner"
          goal "Add a note to the card"

          attribute :note, CardNote

          sets :note

          emits "CardAnnotated"
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
